_about: Orchestra limits, one place. Each has its reason. Env vars ORCHESTRA_<KEY> (upper case) override for a single run. The runner checks every value on load: a missing key or a value of the wrong shape (type, list items, a bad regex) logs `config: <key> ...` in .review/runner.log and falls back to orchestra/config_defaults.json, which holds today's values; an unreadable file falls back wholesale. Edit this file, not that one.
_infra_retries: Retries only for timeout / no report / lane missing. Thomas, 2,006 reports: a re-run FAIL never came back PASS (5 of 5 ended PARTIAL). PARTIAL/FAIL park and need a task edit.
_backoff_min: Wait before the one infra retry, so a transient outage can clear.
_timeout_s: Starting guess only. After timeout_min_runs finished runs of a weight, the timeout becomes timeout_p95_factor x p95 of those runs (never under timeout_floor_s).
_timeout_ceiling_s: Upper bound on the computed lane timeout (timeout_for: the starting guess and timeout_p95_factor x p95 alike). Without it slow runs raised their own limit: heavy was 10,221 s on 10 Nov 2026 (p95 3,407 s), past the scheduler's 2 h ExecutionTimeLimit, so Windows ended the tick first and the run came back NO_REPORT (audit 10 Nov 2026, O3). Chosen so one tick fits inside $ExecutionTimeLimitMinutes in orchestra/install_task.ps1 (120 min = 7200 s): 3600 ceiling + 900 tick_watchdog_extra_s + 600 gate_timeout_s (gate) + 900 review_timeout_s (reviewer) + 600 gate_timeout_s (run_checks --fast in the integration tree) + 360 worst-case Don consult (consult_busy_wait_s 120 + consult_timeout_s 180 + consult_notes_timeout_s 60) = 6960 s, 240 s spare. 3600 is also the heavy starting guess, and 90 of the last 92 heavy runs finished inside it. orchestra/test_gate_timeout.py fails if ceiling + watchdog extra no longer fits that limit.
_gate_timeout_s: The runner re-runs the task's gate before merging. A gate that times out is broken, not passed.
_broken_gate_codes: Gate exit codes that mean a broken gate, not a failed one: pytest found no tests (5), command not found (127 sh, 9009 cmd).
_maint_share: Maintenance tasks get at most this share of the day's runtime, plus the floor so they aren't starved at midnight. Atrium spent 72% on itself on 29 Oct.
_stale_days: Older tasks assume code that has moved. Re-date the task if it still holds.
_parallel_lanes: One task per lane at the same time (claude + codex + gemini), each with its own lock; state saves merge and merges/pushes take turns. Task Scheduler must allow parallel instances. false = one task at a time.
_lane_slots: How many tasks of one lane may run at once, normally. A campaign (.review/campaign.json, see orchestra/campaign.py) may raise it until its stop_at; the Max-plan sprint (Claude 3, 2-4 Nov 2026) ended Wed 4 Nov 18:00 London; these are the normal values again.
_lane_fallback: A hint for orchestra/lane_pick.py (11 Nov 2026), not the only option: while a lane can't run (limited, see limit_patterns below, or over the spend cap) an explicit-lane task may move to this lane (lane_pick_explicit_scope "hint"), and for Lane: auto it is a tie-break (lane_pick_weights.fallback_hint). Never with Lane-Fixed: yes. The fallback lane's slots still apply. {} turns it off.

copilot: Your full instructions are in the file {prompt-file}. Read that file first and follow it exactly.

_lane_argv: Each lane's command; the prompt goes in on stdin. {npm-shim:<name>} = full path of npm's <name>.cmd if found (the scheduled task's PATH has no %APPDATA%\npm), else <name>. {npm:<package>:<bin>} = that global npm CLI's JS entry, run with node; the lane is left out if it isn't installed. .review/lanes.json still overrides or adds lanes. Why each flag: comment above lane_argv in runner.py (claude stream-json for the live watch; codex full access and MCP off, Chuen 2 Nov 2026; gemini auto_edit = edits, no shell).
_npm_dirs: Where global npm CLIs (codex, copilot, gemini) are looked for, in order, by the lanes ({npm-shim:..}, {npm:..}), orchestra/exams and the agent hub: one list for all three. %VAR% and ~ are expanded, * globs; an entry whose variable is unset is skipped. The scheduled task's PATH has no %APPDATA%\npm, and npm installs made from the Claude desktop app live in its packaged AppData (3 Nov 2026: the daily exams logged copilot skipped: Copilot CLI not found).
_copilot_lane: copilot: -p only points at {prompt-file} (<worktree>/.review/prompt.md, the full prompt), so no long prompt reaches cmd.exe. --add-dir {repo-path:.venv} grants only the repo's venv, resolved at runtime through junctions/symlinks: the worktree links to the main venv outside its allowed paths, which denied Python execution on 6 Nov 2026. --allow-all-tools without --allow-all-paths keeps access to the worktree, temp and that venv; no --allow-all-urls; built-in GitHub MCP off and git push / gh denied so it cannot post as Chuen; the pre-push hook refuses pushes anyway (ORCHESTRA_WORKTREE is set).
_unpriced_lanes: Lanes that report no cost, so the daily spend cap never blocks them.

copilot: (out of|exhausted|no remaining|used (all|up)( of)?)( your)? (premium requests|ai credits)

_limit_patterns: A lane's usage limit is come-back-later, not a failed attempt (2 Nov 2026: Codex's limit message was logged NO_REPORT and spent the retry). Case-insensitive regexes per lane, checked against the last limit_tail_lines lines of the lane log after a run with no report; a lane not listed is checked against all of them. The lane waits until the time the message names, else limit_default_min minutes.
auth_fix_hint: sign-in expired: open a terminal, run the lane's CLI (e.g. `claude`) and sign in (`/login`)
_auth_patterns: A run that dies because the lane's CLI isn't signed in (3 Nov 2026, 18:06: Claude's OAuth sign-in expired and 9 tasks were parked as NO_REPORT in an hour) is treated like a usage limit: the attempt isn't counted and the lane waits auth_retry_min before the next try. Patterns are case-insensitive regexes against the tail of the lane log. A reviewer that can't sign in parks the PASS for a --merge-only re-run instead of blocking it.
_daily_spend_cap_usd_note: The normal cap. The sprint's $400 (2 Nov 2026: spare Claude allowance before it resets; claude -p's total_cost_usd is notional on his plan) was a campaign override; the sprint ended Wed 4 Nov 18:00 London, so $5 applies again.
_daily_spend_cap_usd: Summed from claude -p total_cost_usd. Runs killed before reporting are charged an estimate from minutes x today's cost per minute. Thomas's ledger saw under half of a 20-hour spend.
_tick_gap_counts_as_downtime_s: Ticks come every 2 minutes (install_task.ps1). A gap between two ticks longer than this is the laptop off or asleep: it is recorded in .review/<uptime_file> and a lane's time inside it is never charged (11 Nov 2026: a restart at 18:47 left two Claude lanes dead until the 22:46 tick, which charged ~$650 estimated for 4 h nobody ran and filled the daily cap). 900 = several missed ticks, so one slow tick is not downtime. A lane's charged time is also capped at its own timeout, and a lane that started before the last Windows boot (GetTickCount64) is charged only up to that boot.
_uptime_file: Under .review/: the last tick's time and the downtime gaps found (tick_gap_counts_as_downtime_s), kept downtime_keep_days.
_downtime_keep_days: Downtime gaps older than this are dropped from uptime_file: no lane runs longer than a day, so three days is plenty.
_lost_to_restart_status: The result word for a lane found dead with no report after Windows booted since it started (the restart killed it). It is not an attempt: it does not use up infra_retries, has no backoff, and is re-run lost_to_restart_retries times; after that a further loss is NO_REPORT as usual.
_done_window_days: A task whose exact content already PASSed within this window is not run again (content hash, not title: titles get reused).
_status_by_prompt_days: Lookback window for status.py's review-prompt version summary.
_status_recent_runs: How many recent lane runs status.py displays.
_vault_dir: Each finished task gets a section in <vault>/Calendar/Orchestra/<date>.md, committed in the vault repo (Chuen, 2 Nov 2026). Empty string turns it off.
_vault_lock: Every Orchestra write into the vault (day note, hot.md waiting block, STATE NOW.md) and the vault repo's git add/commit take one lock: .review/<vault_lock_name> (orchestra/vaultlock.py). A holder whose pid is gone is taken over at once; any lock older than vault_lock_stale_s (longer than two 120 s git calls) is taken over too. A tick waits up to vault_lock_wait_s, checking every vault_lock_poll_s, then gives up for this tick (audit 10 Nov 2026, O6: parallel ticks dropped each other's day-note sections).
_admission_forbidden_prefixes: Admission rejects any scope path whose repo-relative form starts with one of these prefixes; they are runtime, git, venv or policy directories.
_admission_policy_files: Policy files the local-team admission layer may never scope; a task cannot route into its own enforcement layer.
_admission_remembered_kinds: Refusal kinds that block the same evidence later; admission.py keeps them as a dedupe set.
_admission_stop_words: Stop words stripped from task titles before de-duping and goal overlap checks; a generic title gets rejected as too unhelpful.
_campaign_paused_status: Status text used when a campaign is paused; the runner and display output show this exact wording.
_campaign_ended_status: Status text used when a campaign has no live override but the runner still remembers the campaign.
_campaign_schedule_disabled_status: Status text used when the scheduler is disabled; the runner returns this exact wording.
_campaign_cancelled_status: Status text used when a task is parked as cancelled by Chuen in an emergency-stop flow.
_campaign_stopped_by_chuen_status: Status text shown in a campaign summary when Chuen has ended the active sprint.
_auto_push: After a merge the runner (never the task session) pushes the default branch, unless the checkout is mid-merge, origin is ahead, or the commits touch private-looking paths or add key-like strings. The repo is public. false turns it off.
_review_risky: Before integration, a diff with a changed path matching review_risky_patterns (regexes: orchestra/, atrium/hook.py, .git/hooks, an install_*.ps1), or over review_max_lines changed lines, gets a fresh read-only reviewer (reviewer_argv, unless .review/lanes.json has a "reviewer" lane; prompt: orchestra/review_diff_prompt.md, the diff cut at review_diff_max_chars). VERDICT: block, no verdict, a timeout or a missing lane parks the task. Its cost counts like any lane. false turns it off.
_conflict_hot_files: orchestra/conflicts.py. A runnable task whose predicted files (paths in its body, the learned map in .review/<conflict_map_file>, seeded from master's last conflict_bootstrap_merges merges; title words of at least conflict_min_word_len letters, not conflict_stop_words, vote and a file scoring conflict_map_threshold is predicted) overlap a running task's changed or predicted files on one of these is held while another runnable task without an overlap exists; a name without a slash matches any file of that name. After conflict_max_holds holds it runs anyway (never starved). Paths under conflict_ignore_prefixes are never predicted. Log: 'held <slug>: overlaps <other> on <file>'. 2 Nov 2026: six PASSes failed to merge, mostly on these files.
_conflict_followup: After a PASS hits a merge conflict, or its combined tree fails while both sides changed the same files (up to conflict_both_sides_shown named), queue one <slug><conflict_followup_suffix> task from orchestra/merge_followup_prompt.md (Lane conflict_followup_lane, Priority conflict_followup_priority, Merge-Of header): merge review/<slug> onto current master keeping both sides, re-run the original gate. When it merges, the original is marked 'merged by ...' and, if parked, archived. If the follow-up fails too it parks for a person. false = only park, as before.
_dispatch_on_battery: Master prompt section 8: pause heavy background work on battery. false = on battery the runner starts no new lane (logs ON BATTERY at most every 30 min); running lanes finish and a finished lane is still gated, merged and pushed. true = dispatch on battery until battery_floor_percent, then stop starting lanes. Running lanes are never killed for power. Task Scheduler no longer stops ticks on unplug (install_task.ps1, 2 Nov 2026).

power_override_text.granted: One-task battery override granted {target}; void at {expires} ({minutes} min) if unused.
power_override_text.not_needed: Nothing to override: power is {power}. No grant written.
power_override_text.refused_floor: Refused: battery at {pct}%, at or under the {floor}% floor. No grant written.
power_override_text.expired_log: POWER: one-task override {target} expired unused; cleared
power_override_text.pending_line: one-task override pending {target}, granted by {who}, void at {expires}
power_override_text.expired_line: one-task override {target} expired at {expires} (unused; cleared next tick)

_power_override: One-task battery override (Chuen, 9 Nov 2026). `orchestra/power.py allow-once [--task <slug>] [--lane <lane>] [--why ...]` writes .review/<power_override_file> (who, when, why, optional task and lane) only while dispatch_on_battery blocks dispatch and the battery is above battery_floor_percent. The next tick on battery starts exactly ONE new lane (that task/lane, else the top runnable task), deletes the grant under the dispatch lock and logs used_log; every other lane still waits, running lanes are never killed, config.json is never edited. Unused, it is void after power_override_minutes and cleared. On AC the grant is left alone. The last use (.review/<power_override_used_file>) shows in STATE NOW and watch.py for power_override_minutes. `power.py status` shows a pending grant. Wording: power_override_text.
_auto_admit_areas: Areas (orchestra/gates.json) whose local-team tasks admission.py writes as Queue: auto. Empty = every local-team task lands as Queue: draft and a Claude chat or check-in promotes it. Add e.g. "orchestra" once its drafts have earned it.
_producer_queue_cap: admission.py refuses a new task while .review/queue/ holds this many, and after this many admissions in the last hour. Duplicates are checked against queued, parked and archived tasks and earlier admissions/refusals within producer_dedupe_days.
_producer_target_ready: The producer (python -m orchestra.local_team produce, every 30 min) scans for new work only while the queue has fewer than this many tasks, plans at most producer_plans_per_run candidates, and reads at most producer_librarian_per_run new reports per run.
_local_team_model: Installed Ollama model only; the local team never pulls one. num_ctx matches Denisse's DENISSE_NUM_CTX so the loaded model is reused, not reloaded. A call is skipped (not queued) if nvidia-smi says the GPU is at least local_team_gpu_busy_pct busy, another model is loaded, or .review/gpu.lease is held; a lease older than gpu_lease_ttl_s or whose pid is gone is stale.
_exams_daily_at: Once a day, at the first tick after this time, the runner starts one canary exam per agent (orchestra/exams/daily.py) in a hidden background process with its own lock (.review/exams.lock) and a total cap of exams_cap_s, so routing (orchestra/exams/lane_for.py) runs on real scores. Skipped while any lane is limited, on battery, or paused; it never takes a lane slot. claude only with exams_include_claude: true (Chuen's allowance). Empty string turns it off.
_taskkill_timeout_s: Maximum wait for Windows taskkill when stopping a lane process tree.
_process_exit_wait_timeout_s: Grace period for a killed lane process to exit before treating it as timed out.
_tick_watchdog_extra_s: The whole tick is killed this long after the longest possible lane timeout. Atrium hung 19 then 29 minutes on one call.
keep_ref_log: KEPT {branch}: {count} commit(s) not on master saved as {ref} before {why}; recover with `git branch <name> {ref}`
merge_only_paragraph: {mark} the work for this task is already on branch `{branch}` but never reached master. The runner merges that branch onto current master itself and re-runs the gate below (plus the reviewer, if the diff is risky); no new lane runs. If the branch is missing or the merge can't run, the task is parked. Re-queued {when}{note}.
merge_only_report:
RESULT: PASS
GATE: re-run by the runner before the merge
HUMAN: none
PREMISE: not stated
DONE:
- merge-only re-queue: the runner merged the existing branch {branch}; no lane ran
merge_only_park: merge-only re-queue not merged: {why}. No lane was run; branch {branch} kept if it exists
merge_only_gate_skipped: skipped: merge-only re-queue, so no lane ran on {branch} and its own gate was not re-run on the old tree; the task's gate runs on {branch} merged onto current master in integration
merge_only_on_master: already on master: every commit of {branch} is on the default branch, so there is nothing to gate or merge
merge_landed: landed on master (branch tip on master, or branch gone)
_merge_only_gate_skipped: merge_only_gate_skipped: a merge-only run skips the gate on the old branch (it can be days behind master; 9 Nov 2026 four re-queues failed a test master had already fixed) and relies on integration's combined-tree gate. merge_only_on_master: a merge-only branch whose commits are all on master is archived as done with this note, ungated. merge_landed: the state's merge note once a 'PASS not merged' branch's tip is on master or the branch is gone; the waiting lists (STATE_NOW, hot.md) drop it.
_keep_ref_prefix: Before the runner deletes or resets a review/<slug> branch (a fresh worktree, cleanup), any commits it has that aren't on master are saved as <keep_ref_prefix><slug>-<UTC time> and logged with keep_ref_log. Twice in the week of 2 Nov 2026 a branch with reviewed, unmerged commits was deleted (time-tasks-2 came back only via git fsck). merge_only_* : a requeue.py --merge-only task (its body has a line starting with merge_only_mark) is merged by the runner from the existing branch -- gate, reviewer, combined-tree integration -- and never runs a lane; a missing branch or a merge that can't run parks it with merge_only_park.
_consult_narrow_to: The widest consult_applies may be in effect, without editing it: "" = no narrowing (consult_applies as written), "named" = all is treated as named (only a task whose header says Consult: don or whose text names the study tooling is put to the tutor), "off" = no consult. Named keeps the 5 Nov rule (a professional opinion on study work). Back to every task: set "".
_live_window_with_lane_tab: false = a lane that gets its own tab (lane_tabs, lane_tab_lanes) does not also open the live window: one window per run, not two. A lane without a tab still opens it (live_window), and `python orchestra/watch.py` opens it by hand any time. Why (task 2026-11-12T0104 'Orchestra back to Thomas's base rules', docs/orchestra_vs_thomas.md): 11-12 Nov 2026 runner.log has a LIVE window opened line beside nearly every LANE tab opened line (19 and 19), so each task put two windows on the desktop for Chuen to close; the tab already shows the lane working (his 9 Nov ask). true = both, as before.
_consult_applies: Which tasks the study tutor (Don) is asked about before their lane starts, any lane: all = every task (Chuen, 9 Nov 2026: every agent goes through Don); named = only a task whose header says Consult: don or whose text names the study tooling (consult.json path_patterns); off = none. Advisory either way: the lane may disagree and says so under ODD. consult_timeout_s caps the full consult (local model, Claude for a hard topic); consult_notes_timeout_s the notes-only one (python -m tutor consult --notes-only: no model). Before the full consult the runner checks the GPU: the gpu.lease held by another job, or nvidia-smi at least consult_gpu_busy_pct busy, is busy; it waits up to consult_busy_wait_s (polling every consult_busy_poll_s), then, with consult_notes_fallback, takes the notes-only path instead, as it does when the full consult fails. The log line says which path was used.
_live_window: Visible runs (Chuen, 9 Nov 2026: 'I want to see Claude Code running'). live_window: when a lane starts, one console window titled live_window_title running orchestra/watch.py is opened if none is open already (its pid is kept in .review/live_window.json), shown without taking focus; never a second one. {python} is the runner's interpreter, {watch} watch.py. toasts: a Windows toast at each lane start and finish, from toast_started / toast_finished, sent by orchestra/toast.ps1 ({script}) with {text}; a toast that fails or takes over toast_timeout_s is ignored.
_hub_queue_default_gate: The agent hub's queue_task (orchestra/agent_hub/server.mjs) hands work to Orchestra through orchestra/new_task.py with Queue: auto and From: hub_queue_source; a task given no gate gets hub_queue_default_gate.
_lane_tabs: Each lane run in its own Windows Terminal tab titled lane_tab_title ("Claude: <task title>"), in the wt window named lane_tab_window, for the lanes in lane_tab_lanes (Chuen, 9 Nov 2026: he wants to watch Claude Code work). The lane itself stays headless claude -p stream-json, so the report file, timeout, kill-on-close job, cost capture, worktree, guard hook and Don consult are unchanged: the tab (orchestra/lane_tab.py) only renders <slug>.lane.log the way Claude Code does (text, each tool call with its file or command, Edit/Write diffs, the result). When the lane exits the runner writes <slug>.lane.done; the tab prints lane_tab_done_text and closes after lane_tab_linger_s; with no DONE it stops after the timeout + lane_tab_extra_s. No wt.exe: the same renderer in a plain console if lane_tab_fallback_console. false = no tabs (the one live window and the toasts still follow live_window / toasts).
lane_tab_done_text: DONE ({result}). The runner now re-runs the gate and merges a PASS; this tab closes in {linger} s.
lane_tab_max_text: Stopped following: the runner never said DONE (it may have been killed). Closing.
_bugfix_kinds: Chuen, 9 Nov 2026: "whenever there's bugs and errors use Claude Code". A task whose Kind: is one of bugfix_kinds scores bugfix_lane_bonus more on bugfix_lane (orchestra/lane_pick.py, 11 Nov 2026: a weight, no longer an override), so it goes there while that lane can run and isn't held at its reserve; never with Lane-Fixed: yes. Logged on the START line as bugfix_route_note. "" for bugfix_lane turns the rule off.
_lane_auto_word: A task header `Lane: <this word>` (new_task.py's default) has its lane picked at dispatch by orchestra/lane_pick.py (Chuen, 11 Nov 2026: "I want everything softcoded, where the agents auto-task"). An explicit `Lane: X` is a preference worth lane_preference_bonus; `Lane-Fixed: yes` never moves. The pick goes in the task header (lane_pick_headers), runner.log (`PICK <slug> -> <lane>: <why>`), the history entry (lane_asked, pick_why) and the hub's task table. `runner.py --dry-run` prints the scores per lane; `python -m orchestra.lane_pick explain <slug>` prints the reasoning.
_lane_pick_yes_words: Header values that mean yes (Lane-Fixed: yes).
_lane_pick_headers: The header lines the runner writes into a dispatched task whose lane it picked. Left out of the task's content hash, so recording a pick never makes it a different task.
_lane_work_header: Optional task header naming the work kind for lane_strengths (code-edit, debug, writing, study, extract, review). Without it: lane_work_for_kind by the task's Kind, else the title's category (orchestra/exams/rules.json title_routes, the rules new_task.py used), else lane_work_default.
_lane_work_for_kind: Work kind by the task's Kind: header, before the title is looked at.
_lane_work_default: Work kind when nothing else says: most Orchestra tasks edit code.
_lane_strengths: Fit per lane per work kind, 0..1 (weighted by lane_pick_weights.fit). Seeded 11 Nov 2026 from the routing so far: claude was the default lane for every kind the exams had no measured answer for (code-edit, debug, writing, study; rules.json default_lane) and bug fixes went to claude (bugfix_lane); the exams' only measured category, extract, had codex and copilot at 100% (Dev/Agent-Scores.md, 11 Nov); copilot took tasks only when named; gemini can edit but not run a shell (lane_argv). Re-score as the exams measure more.
_lane_strength_default: Fit of a lane or work kind not listed in lane_strengths (a new lane, a test lane).
_lane_preference_bonus: Score for the lane an explicit `Lane: X` names: the named lane's own pacing isn't counted (naming it is Chuen's pacing call), and with lane_pick_explicit_scope "hint" only being unavailable (limited, over the spend cap) or the bug-fix bonus moves the task.
_bugfix_lane_bonus: Was an override (bugfix_lane took every bug fix; Chuen, 9 Nov 2026: "whenever there's bugs and errors use Claude Code"), now a weight: a bug fix scores this much more on bugfix_lane. More than lane_preference_bonus, so bug fixes still go to claude while it can run; when claude is limited, over the cap or held at its reserve (lane_pacing), a bug fix goes to another lane.
_lane_pick_weights: How much each part of a lane's score counts: fit (lane_strengths), pacing (lane_pacing, -1..1), cost (share of daily_spend_cap_usd spent, priced lanes only), busy (no free slot in lane_slots), fallback_hint (the asked or best-fit lane's lane_fallback while that lane can't run: a tie-break, not the only option).
_lane_pick_explicit_scope: Where an explicit `Lane: X` may go: "hint" = only to bugfix_lane (for a bug fix) or, while X can't run, to lane_fallback[X] (today's rules, scored); "any" = any lane, scored. `Lane: auto` is always scored over every lane.
_lane_pacing: Per lane: one reset time (reset_anchor; later resets every period_h hours), the last spend_window_h hours before it when the lane is spent freely (use it or lose it), and the share of the allowance to keep (reserve). Outside that window a lane is spent in proportion to the time left: more left than the time left -> plus, less -> minus; at or under reserve it is held (not picked unless the header names it). reserve 1 keeps it all until the window. Replaces two hand rules: "hold Codex until the last hours before its weekly reset" (hub, 10 Nov 2026; its limit message reset 11 Nov 12:08) and "pause Claude near its weekly limit" (reserve 0.1; the reset anchor is the Max-plan sprint's end, Wed 4 Nov 18:00, since no reset time is recorded: correct it when known). A lane not listed has no pacing. Allowance used comes from lane_usage_file; with none it is unknown, not used up.
_lane_free_above_left: Chuen, 11 Nov 2026: "the holding back only applies if the weekly limit is less than 20%; if it's not, use them freely". Share of a lane's weekly allowance left at or above which lane_pacing neither holds nor paces it (unknown usage counts as not low); below it reserve and pacing apply. A lane_pacing entry may set its own free_above_left.
_lane_usage_file: Optional .review/<file>: {"<lane>": {"used": 0.8 (or "left": 0.2), "reset": "<ISO time, overrides reset_anchor>", "at": "<ISO time seen>"}}. Missing, unreadable or a lane not in it: usage unknown. Limits seen in lane logs are separate (state lanes.<lane>.limited_until, limit_patterns).
_lane_usage_max_age_h: A lane_usage_file entry older than this (by its "at") counts as unknown. 0 = never stale.
_reviewer_lanes: Lanes that can review a risky diff, each with its read-only argv ([] = reviewer_argv). The reviewer is picked like a task lane (lane_strengths for reviewer_work, lane_pacing as a weight, cost, limits) and is never the lane that wrote the change (independent review); no other lane able to run now = the PASS parks as REVIEW-UNAVAILABLE for a --merge-only re-run. codex: read-only sandbox, plain text output. The runner frames each prompt with fresh runtime boundaries: parse_verdict discards echoed input through its closing boundary before parsing JSON or plain text, and blocks an incomplete echo or no reviewer verdict. .review/lanes.json's reviewer_override_lane entry still overrides all of this.
_reviewer_work: The lane_strengths work kind a reviewer pick is scored by.
_reviewer_override_lane: The .review/lanes.json entry that, if present, is the reviewer for every change (tests, a manual override). Never picked as a task lane.
_autopilot: When no Queue: auto task is left, the laptop is on AC and a lane has allowance, the planner (atrium/autopilot.py) writes the next tasks through new_task.create from autopilot_sources: inbox (autopilot_inbox_note, under autopilot_inbox_heading), not_done / odd (reports of the last autopilot_report_days), parked (not those matching autopilot_parked_skip_patterns), waiting (hot.md, outside Orchestra's own block). The local model (autopilot_classifier "model": autopilot_model at autopilot_model_url) reads each one; with no answer the autopilot_fallback_actionable rule applies and the task is a draft. Queue: auto only when the model says repo-only and autopilot_gate can run; else draft, listed in hot.md. Caps: autopilot_max_per_hour / _per_day / _per_refill; no two tasks on the same files (conflicts.py's predictor); nothing open, parked or done in the last autopilot_dedupe_days. Lane: the one in autopilot_lanes with allowance (not LIMITED, spend cap not reached) and the fewest runs in autopilot_balance_hours; bug fixes (the model says so, or a PARTIAL/FAIL source in autopilot_bugfix_results) to bugfix_lane. Every decision is one AUTOPILOT line in runner.log; the ledger is .review/autopilot.json. false = off.
_autopilot_sources_off: Sources in autopilot_sources the planner does not read, without editing that list. Why (task 2026-11-12T0104 'Orchestra back to Thomas's base rules', docs/orchestra_vs_thomas.md): .review/README.md leaves out, on purpose, tasks generated from log errors. not_done / odd are lines of the lanes' own reports and parked is the runner's park reason: all three are Orchestra's output fed back in as new work. 12 Nov 2026 00:44: two Follow-up tasks were written from a three-day-old report's NOT DONE list; one pushed 3 commits nobody asked for, the other came back NO_REPORT twice and was parked for Chuen. inbox and waiting stay: those are his own words. [] = every source in autopilot_sources is read again.
autopilot_body:
{text}

Written by Orchestra's autopilot planner from {source} ({origin}); {context}.
Planner: {why}.

Check the premise first: this came from a note and the code may have moved. If any part would send as Chuen, spend, delete something that can't be recovered, sign in, or touch the vault outside tests, do the rest and put that one question on the HUMAN line.
_master_health: Master's own health (orchestra/master_health.py; audit 10 Nov 2026, H1). One test red on master made every session PARTIAL whatever it worked on: 6 tasks on 4 Nov (a config default out of step), 7 on 5 Nov (a test that failed on Thursdays). The runner keeps one record per master commit of master_health_baseline's result; while the record for master's current commit is red, why_not_runnable holds every task whose Kind: is not in bugfix_kinds, and one urgent bug-fix task is written. An unchecked commit counts as green. false = off: nothing is checked or held.
_master_health_file: The record, under .review/: commit -> status (green / red / broken), the modules that did not pass, the output's tail, when, how long, and how (a baseline run, or the combined tree before a fast-forward).
_master_health_lock: Under .review/: held by the one baseline run allowed at a time; stale after master_health_timeout_s per baseline command plus master_health_lock_grace_s (the child died).
_master_health_lock_grace_s: Slack on top of the baseline's own timeout before its lock counts as stale: worktree add/remove and the venv link take seconds, a loaded laptop more.
_master_health_keep: Records kept (oldest dropped): master moves a few dozen times a day at most, and only the current commit and a branch's base are ever read.
_master_health_head_cache_s: why_not_runnable runs for every queued task each tick (and for STATE_NOW): master's commit is read once per this many seconds, not one git call per task.
_master_health_baseline: The baseline command(s), run through the shell in a detached worktree of the master commit, venv linked. [] = hub_queue_default_gate, the same run_checks --fast line the hub and autopilot give every task, so 'red' means exactly what would fail every task's gate.
_master_health_timeout_s: Per baseline command. run_checks --fast takes about 1-2 min here; a run that times out is recorded broken (not red: no module to name), which holds nothing.
_master_health_worktree_prefix: The baseline worktree's folder in the worktrees folder: <prefix><first 12 of the commit>, removed after the run like the integration tree.
_master_health_log_file: The last baseline run's full output, under .review/reports/.
_master_health_module_patterns: How the modules that did not pass are read from the output: run_checks.py prints '--- <module> (<STATUS>, exit N) ---' before each one that did not pass. Each regex needs (?P<module>) and (?P<status>) groups. Only these lines count, never warnings in the output; if none match, the record keeps the tail and says master_health_unparsed.
_master_health_pass_statuses: run_checks statuses that count as passed (with --verbose it prints a header for those too).
_master_health_tail_lines: Lines of a red or broken run's output kept in the record and the bug-fix task.
_master_health_unparsed_holds: A baseline that fails without naming a module (no line matched master_health_module_patterns) is recorded broken, keeps its tail and holds nothing: it may not have run at all (the soak, 10 Nov 2026: cmd.exe could not find .venv\Scripts\python.exe, exit 1, and master was held red on the environment, not on master). true = record it red and hold, saying master_health_unparsed.
_master_health_broken_retry_min: A broken record (timed out, or failed naming no module) is checked again after this long: a loaded laptop or a missing link may have been the cause, not master.
master_health_unparsed: (failing modules not named in the output; see the tail in .review/master_health.json)
_master_health_unparsed: Said instead of module names when the baseline failed but no line matched master_health_module_patterns.
_master_health_hold: why_not_runnable's reason for a held task (STATE_NOW's queue lists it).
_master_health_log_every_s: The MASTER RED log line at most once per this many seconds per commit, not every 2-minute tick (as ON BATTERY).
master_health_red_log: MASTER RED {commit}: holding every task but bug fixes (Kind: {kinds}): {modules}
_master_health_red_log: runner.log line while master is red (throttled).
_master_health_start_log: runner.log line when a baseline run starts in the background.
_master_health_done_log: runner.log line the background run writes when it is done.
master_health_task_log: MASTER RED {commit}: wrote bug-fix task {task} for {modules}
_master_health_task_log: runner.log line when the bug-fix task is written.
_master_health_task_title: The bug-fix task's title. One per red commit, and never while a Queue: auto bug-fix task is open.
_master_health_task_priority: Every other task waits on it.
_master_health_task_weight: The red-master fixes so far were one commit each (the 4 Nov config default, the 5 Nov Thursday clock).
_master_health_combined_marks_green: After a fast-forward, the commit the combined tree just tested is recorded green without a second run when one of its checks starts with this (check_combined's label for run_checks --fast). Only right while master_health_baseline is that same line: set "" if the baseline changes.
master_health_park_note: Master was already red at this branch's base {commit} on {modules} (orchestra/master_health.py).
_master_health_park_note: Added to a park reason when the branch's base commit has a red record, so the next reader knows.
master_health_park_only: The runner's gate failed only on those modules: this branch is not at fault.
_master_health_park_only: Added after master_health_park_note when the runner's own gate log (from this run) names failing modules and all of them were red at the base.
master_health_state_red: **Master:** RED at {commit}: {modules}. Only bug fixes run; bug-fix task: {task}.
_master_health_state_red: STATE_NOW's line while master is red.
_master_health_state_known: STATE_NOW's line when master's commit has a green or broken record.
master_health_state_unknown: **Master:** {commit} not checked yet ({running}); counts as green.
_master_health_state_unknown: STATE_NOW's line when master's commit has no record.
